text: Be extremely upon your guard against vanity, the common failing of inexperienced youth; but particularly against that kind of vanity that dubs a man a coxcomb; a character which, once acquired, is more indelible than that of the priesthood.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXIII, to his son, London, May 17, Old Style 1750
